title: Pipeline bar segments are interactive divs with no keyboard access or ARIA roles
detail: Lines 162-178: each pipeline segment is a <div> with onClick and mouse handlers but no role='button', no tabIndex, and no keyboard event handler. Screen readers cannot navigate these, and keyboard-only users cannot click them. Each segment navigates to /contracts?status=N so this is functional content, not decorative.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:163 `<div key={status} ... onClick={() => navigate(...)}` — no role, tabIndex, or onKeyDown.
recommendedFix: Add `role='button'` and `tabIndex={0}` to each pipeline segment div. Add `onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') navigate(...); }}` for keyboard activation.

title: Pipeline legend color swatches lack alt text for color-blind users
detail: Line 183: each legend entry uses a colored <span> as the only indicator of which pipeline segment it refers to. The status text is adjacent but there is no programmatic association between the swatch and the label. Users who cannot distinguish the colors (e.g., #34D399 green vs #60A5FA blue) rely solely on the text ordering to match legend to bar, which is fragile if the bar order differs from legend order.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:183 — colored span has no aria-label or role='img' with alt.
recommendedFix: Add `role='img'` and `aria-label={STATUS_LABELS[status]}` to each legend color swatch span. This is a low-effort a11y improvement.

title: KpiTile is a clickable div with no keyboard accessibility
detail: Lines 302-328: KpiTile renders an onClick div with hover effects and cursor:pointer but no role='button', no tabIndex, and no onKeyDown handler. Three KPI tiles on the dashboard navigate to /contracts and /send-queue. Keyboard-only users cannot reach or activate these tiles.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:305 `onClick={onClick}` on a plain <div> — no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handler.
recommendedFix: Add `role='button'`, `tabIndex={0}`, and `onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') onClick(); }}` to the KpiTile root div.

title: Dead code: `fmt` and `btnStyles` are defined but never used
detail: Line 375: function `fmt(val)` formats currency but is never called in SalesDashboard. Line 391: `btnStyles.primary` object is defined but never referenced. Both are dead code from a prior iteration of the dashboard that displayed budget data directly.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:375 `function fmt(val)`, line 391 `const btnStyles`. grep for 'fmt(' and 'btnStyles' in this file returns only the definitions.
recommendedFix: Remove both `fmt` function (lines 375-378) and `btnStyles` constant (lines 391-399).

title: Onboarding status badge uses hardcoded magic number 100000001
detail: Line 211: `c.dcfg_status === 100000001 ? 'In Progress' : 'New'` uses a raw integer. The same constant exists as OnboardingCaseStatus.InProgress in portalApi.js but is not imported here. Magic numbers in production UI code are fragile and hard to trace.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:211 and 212 — raw `100000001` comparisons for status badge styling.
recommendedFix: Import OnboardingCaseStatus from portalApi.js and use `OnboardingCaseStatus.InProgress` instead of the raw number.

title: Activity log contract link uses <a href> instead of navigate() — causes full page reload in SPA
detail: Line 282: `<a href={'/contracts/${log.dcfg_related_contract_id}'}` uses a raw anchor tag. In a HashRouter SPA, this causes a full browser navigation instead of a client-side route transition — losing all in-memory state (loaded data, scroll position, etc.). Every other clickable navigation in SalesDashboard uses `navigate()` correctly.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:282 `View` — should be navigate() or .
recommendedFix: Replace the `<a>` with a `<span>` or `<button>` using `onClick={() => navigate('/contracts/' + log.dcfg_related_contract_id)}`, or use `<Link to={...}>` from react-router-dom.

title: customerMap is built on every render but never consumed
detail: Line 102: `const customerMap = Object.fromEntries(customers.map(...))` builds a lookup map on every render. The comment says 'kept for data layer compatibility' but no code in the file reads from customerMap. This is a small per-render allocation that adds up on re-renders.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:102 — customerMap defined, grep for 'customerMap' in this file returns only the definition line.
recommendedFix: Remove the customerMap computation. If it is needed in the future, wrap it in useMemo.

title: CustomerList useEffect dep on showAll re-fetches entire list on toggle — no $top cap
detail: Line 33: `useEffect(() => { loadCustomers(); }, [showAll]);` re-fetches all customers whenever the 'Show inactive' checkbox toggles. Line 40: the apiGet has no $top cap. At scale this means toggling the checkbox fires an unbounded Dataverse read. Not urgent at current data volume but should have a safety cap.
evidence: CustomerList.jsx:40 — apiGet with no $top. Line 33 — re-fetch on showAll toggle.
recommendedFix: Add `&$top=500` (or an appropriate cap) to the apiGet query string.

title: NewCustomerPanel duplicate check swallows errors silently — catch block is empty
detail: Line 140: `} catch {}` after the duplicate-name check apiGet. If the duplicate check fails (e.g., network error, 403), the empty catch means the code proceeds silently to create the customer WITHOUT the dup warning. The user gets no feedback that the safety check was skipped.
evidence: CustomerList.jsx:140 — empty catch block after duplicate check.
recommendedFix: At minimum log the error. Better: show a non-blocking toast like 'Could not check for duplicates — proceeding with save'.

title: NewCustomerPanel creates customer even after detecting a duplicate — warning shown AFTER creation
detail: Line 139: `if (dup?.value?.length > 0) setDupWarn(...)` sets a warning state, but execution falls through to the creation block at line 141. The customer is created regardless of the duplicate, and the warning message confirms: 'Record was still created.' This is intentional per the comment but the UX is confusing: the user sees a green save + a warning simultaneously. The user should be prompted BEFORE creation to confirm they want a duplicate.
evidence: CustomerList.jsx:136-151 — dup check then unconditional create. Warning says 'Record was still created.'
recommendedFix: Show the duplicate warning BEFORE creating and require user confirmation to proceed. Use a confirm dialog or a two-step flow: check → warn → user clicks 'Save Anyway' → create.

title: Search input lacks an associated <label> for screen readers
detail: Line 56-61: the search input has a placeholder but no associated <label> element or aria-label attribute. Screen readers will announce it as an unlabeled text field. The 'Show inactive' checkbox (line 64) does have a label wrapping it, but the search input does not.
evidence: CustomerList.jsx:56 — <input ... placeholder='Search customers...'> with no aria-label or <label for>.
recommendedFix: Add `aria-label='Search customers'` to the search input.

title: handleSaveEdit has no try/catch — apiPatch failure is an unhandled promise rejection
detail: Lines 58-68: `handleSaveEdit` calls `apiPatch(...)` then `loadCustomer()` but has no try/catch. If the PATCH fails (403, validation error, network timeout), the promise rejects unhandled. The user sees no error feedback — the edit panel stays open with no indication of failure. This is a write operation on customer master data.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:58-68 — async function with await apiPatch but no try/catch or .catch.
recommendedFix: Wrap in try/catch. On catch: `toast.show('err', 'Failed to save: ' + e.message)`. On success: toast.show('ok', 'Customer saved').

title: LOGO_MAP contains customer names as hardcoded keys — violates no-customer-names-in-production rule
detail: Line 30: `const LOGO_MAP = { 'J-ADD':'jadd.png', 'The Arc Mercer':'thearcmercer', 'PennReach':'pennreach.png', 'Bancroft':'decades.png', ... }` hardcodes customer names directly in source code. Per feedback_no_customer_or_people_names_in_production.md, no customer names should appear in production code. The mapping should be stored in Dataverse (e.g., a dcfg_logo_file column on dcfg_customers) or in dcfg_configs.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:30 — LOGO_MAP with customer names as keys.
recommendedFix: Add a `dcfg_logo_file` column to dcfg_customers, populate it per customer, and read the logo filename from the customer record at render time. Remove the hardcoded LOGO_MAP entirely.

title: MsasTab handleNewMsa has no try/catch — apiPost failure crashes silently
detail: Lines 219-231: handleNewMsa calls apiPost then apiGet to refresh. Neither is wrapped in try/catch. If the POST fails (e.g., missing required field, 403), the error is unhandled. The panel closes on line 228 before the re-fetch, so even the refresh error is swallowed. The user sees the panel close but the new MSA does not appear, with no error message.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:219-231 — async function with no try/catch.
recommendedFix: Wrap in try/catch. On error: keep the panel open, show the error in the panel. On success: close panel and refresh.

title: OnboardingTab loadOnboarding has empty catch — all errors silently swallowed
detail: Line 382: `} catch {}` — if any of the three apiGet calls inside loadOnboarding fail, the error is silently discarded. The user sees an empty onboarding tab with no indication that loading failed. This masks permission errors (403) that would indicate a table permissions issue on dcfg_onboarding_cases or dcfg_onboarding_checklists.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:382 — empty catch block in loadOnboarding.
recommendedFix: Capture the error and set an error state that renders a warn-banner in the tab UI, e.g., 'Failed to load onboarding data.'

title: ProgramsTab loadPrograms has no error handling — apiGet failure is unhandled
detail: Lines 496-498: `const r = await apiGet(...)` with no try/catch wrapping. If the dcfg_programs table is unreachable (403, 500), the promise rejects unhandled and the programs tab stays in its initial empty-array state with no error banner.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:496-498 — loadPrograms with no try/catch.
recommendedFix: Add try/catch and set an error state rendered as a warn-banner.

title: ProgramsTab handleNewProgram has no try/catch — creation failure is unhandled
detail: Lines 501-510: handleNewProgram calls apiPost then loadPrograms with no error handling. If the POST fails, the panel closes (line 508 `setShowNew(false)`) but the error goes unhandled. The user thinks the program was created.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:501-510 — async function with no try/catch.
recommendedFix: Wrap in try/catch. On error: keep the panel open and show the error. The downstream NewProgramForm already has saving state (line 566) but the error path is not wired.

title: Customer logo img has empty alt attribute — should describe the image or be marked decorative
detail: Line 85: `` — the alt is empty string which marks the image as decorative. However, the logo visually conveys the customer brand. For screen reader users, the image should have `alt={customer.dcfg_name + ' logo'}` so they understand what the image represents.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:85 — `alt=''` on the customer logo img.
recommendedFix: Change to `alt={customer.dcfg_name + ' logo'}` or a more descriptive alt text.

title: MsaList search input has no aria-label or associated label element
detail: Line 83-89: the search input has placeholder text but no aria-label or label element. Screen readers will announce it as an unlabeled text field.
evidence: MsaList.jsx:83 — <input ... placeholder='Search agreements...'> with no aria-label.
recommendedFix: Add `aria-label='Search agreements'` to the input element.

title: MsaDetail handleSaveEdit has no try/catch — apiPatch failure is unhandled
detail: Lines 95-108: handleSaveEdit calls apiPatch then apiGet to refresh, with no try/catch. If the PATCH fails (e.g., validation error on dcfg_budget_total), the error is unhandled. The editing state remains true but the user gets no feedback. This is a write operation on MSA records.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:95-108 — async function with no try/catch or .catch.
recommendedFix: Wrap in try/catch. On error: `toast.show('err', 'Failed to save: ' + e.message)`. Keep editing=true so the user can retry.

title: Generate MSA button not disabled after generation completes — no success feedback
detail: Lines 64-80: handleGenerate sets generating=true (disabling the button) but after success, it only updates the document URL. There is no toast or success banner. The user clicks 'Generate MSA', sees 'Generating...' briefly, then the button reverts to 'Generate MSA' with no visible confirmation. The only signal is the 'View Document' link appearing if dcfg_document_url becomes non-null, which is subtle.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:64-80 — no toast.show on success. Compare to handleSubmitForApproval (line 83) which at least does a full MSA re-fetch.
recommendedFix: Add `toast.show('ok', 'MSA document generated')` after the re-fetch on line 75.

title: DocumentHistory apiGet has no $select — fetches all columns from dcfg_document_outputs
detail: Line 249: `apiGet('/dcfg_document_outputs?$filter=...')` has no `$select` clause. This fetches every column on dcfg_document_outputs for every document row. The component only uses dcfg_document_outputid, dcfg_generated_at, dcfg_generated_by, dcfg_merge_status, and dcfg_output_file_url. The missing $select pulls unnecessary data over the wire and violates the cat-8a mandate that every apiGet must have $select.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:249 — apiGet with $filter and $orderby but no $select.
recommendedFix: Add `$select=dcfg_document_outputid,dcfg_generated_at,dcfg_generated_by,dcfg_merge_status,dcfg_output_file_url` to the query.

title: MsaDetail initial load fetches dcfg_document_url but MSA documents use dcfg_output_file_url
detail: Line 49: the initial apiGet on dcfg_msas includes `dcfg_document_url` in $select. Line 145 renders a 'View Document' link using `msa.dcfg_document_url`. However, the DocumentHistory sub-component at line 268 uses `dcfg_output_file_url` from dcfg_document_outputs. These are two different columns on two different tables. The dcfg_document_url on the MSA record appears to be a legacy field that may not be populated by the V4 OOXML docgen path, leaving the 'View Document' link permanently broken for V4-generated documents.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:49 — `dcfg_document_url` in $select. Line 145 — rendered. Line 268 — DocumentHistory uses dcfg_output_file_url from a different table.
recommendedFix: Verify whether dcfg_document_url is still populated by the V4 docgen flow. If not, the 'View Document' link should read from the latest dcfg_document_outputs row instead (dcfg_output_file_url). If dcfg_document_url is still populated, document why both paths exist.

title: OverviewTab builds dynamic OData filter with OR clauses for every MSA ID — potential URL length explosion
detail: Line 159: `const filter = msaIds.map(id => '_dcfg_msa_id_value eq ${id}').join(' or ');` builds an OData filter with one OR clause per MSA GUID. Each GUID is 36 characters plus the surrounding clause (~55 chars). A customer with 50 MSAs produces a ~2750 character filter string; at 100 MSAs it approaches the Power Pages URL length limit. The same pattern appears in ContractsTab line 327.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:159-160 — dynamic filter with unbounded OR clauses. Same pattern at line 327.
recommendedFix: For customers with many MSAs, consider batch fetching contracts via multiple requests or use a FetchXML-based approach. At minimum, add a safety cap: if msaIds.length > 50, only query the first 50 or use a different strategy.

title: MsaList apiGet has no $top safety cap — fetches all MSAs unbounded
detail: Line 49: the apiGet for the MSA list has no $top parameter. At scale this will fetch every MSA record in the system. Other list screens (SalesDashboard, CustomerList) have or should have $top caps.
evidence: MsaList.jsx:49 — apiGet with no $top.
recommendedFix: Add `&$top=500` as a safety cap, consistent with SalesDashboard's capped queries.

title: CustomerList table rows with onClick lack keyboard accessibility
detail: Line 91: each <tr> has `onClick={() => navigate(...)}` but table rows have no native keyboard behavior. Users navigating with Tab cannot reach or activate these rows. This pattern repeats in MsaList (line 111) and across all table-based list screens.
evidence: CustomerList.jsx:91 — <tr ... onClick={...}> with no tabIndex or onKeyDown. Same pattern in MsaList.jsx:111.
recommendedFix: Add `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') navigate(...); }}` to each clickable <tr>. Alternatively, wrap the primary column content in a <Link> component.
